I have been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school — everything I know, I learned from my father and from watching what works on the fields around me. I don't trust those outsiders who come with papers and big words. I trust my own two eyes and what Old Wang and the others in my village do.

My land is split: 8 mu I keep for wheat and maize, one after the other. The other 4 mu I plant cotton — cotton needs its own space and can't share with wheat.

For wheat, I plough the 8 mu in October before planting. I use the same improved wheat seed that Old Wang bought from the dealer last year — his crop stood up better to the wind than mine. I put one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, that's the 50 kg bag with the three numbers. Then in spring, when the wheat starts greening up, I spread urea. I use about 30 kg of urea per mu across two times — half at reviving, half at jointing. Last year I cut back and the wheat turned yellow before heading. Never again. Better to spend the money on fertilizer than to lose a whole crop at my age. I water four times from my well: winter irrigation, then at jointing, then when the heads come out, then when the grain is filling. I spray twice for insects and weeds. I expect about 450-500 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

Maize goes in the day after wheat harvest. I don't plough — too slow, and the tractor man charges extra. I hire him to no-till sow straight into the wheat stubble. I use hybrid maize seed, one bag covers about 3 mu. At planting, I put compound fertilizer in the row, about 30 kg per mu. Then when the plants are knee-high, I spread 25 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice from the well in July and August if the rain stays away. Two sprays is enough for maize. I should get around 550-600 jin per mu.

The 4 mu of cotton is more headache. I rotary till that land in April because cotton likes soft ground. I buy improved cotton seed and lay the plastic film — the dealer showed me how, it keeps the soil warm in spring. Cotton needs more potassium, so I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and then top-dress with 20 kg urea twice. I water three times from the well. The bollworm is the real enemy on cotton, so I spray four times, no skipping. I hope for 250-300 jin of seed cotton per mu.

Urea is expensive now, but what can I do? I watch my neighbors. If Old Wang puts more, I put more. If everyone waters, I water. I can't afford to guess wrong. A bad harvest at 67 years old would be the end of me. Better to use a bit too much fertilizer than to go hungry.
